items.issuing_body: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
items.title: FDIC publishes GENIUS Act PPSI reporting forms for PRA comment (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274)
items.facts: On July 20, 2026 (filed on public inspection July 17), the FDIC published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274) requesting 60-day public comment on proposed weekly and quarterly reporting forms for FDIC-supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers (PPSIs). The notice is associated with the FDIC's GENIUS Act PPSI NPRM (April 10, 2026, 91 FR 18534). Weekly Form PS-01 (for PPSIs with $1 billion or more in total outstanding issuance value or $100 million or more in average daily transaction volume) includes eight schedules covering top holders, top exchanges, trading volume, top counterparties, capital, issuance and redemption, and reserve assets disaggregated by type (cash and deposits, U.S. Treasuries by CUSIP, reverse repurchase agreements, money market mutual funds, and other instruments). Weekly Form PS-01a (smaller PPSIs) has three schedules. Quarterly Form PS-02 covers income statement, balance sheet, off-balance sheet items, capital and operational backstop, and memoranda including blockchain activity, redemption metrics, and custody activities. The FDIC estimates approximately 30 FDIC-supervised institutions would perform PPSI activities; ongoing weekly reporting burden estimated at 2,080 hours per year and quarterly at 800 hours. The publication confirms the FDIC GENIUS Act implementing final rule was not published as of the July 18, 2026 statutory one-year deadline. Comment period closes September 18, 2026.
items.source_label: Federal Register — FDIC Notice, FR Doc. 2026-14589 (91 FR 45274), July 20, 2026
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, FDIC-supervised institutions, payment-stablecoin operators, crypto exchanges, compliance counsel

items.issuing_body: Federal Reserve Board
items.title: Fed Chair Warsh testifies to House Financial Services: no Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins; Fed 'racing' to meet GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline; nonbank fintech payment access pressed
items.facts: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the House Committee on Financial Services on July 14, 2026, as part of the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report (2128 Rayburn House Office Building, 10:00 AM). The official prepared statement focused on price stability, monetary policy, and internal Fed task forces. During the Q&A, Warsh made three statements directly relevant to crypto, stablecoin, and fintech operators: (1) No Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins: Pressed by Rep. Brad Sherman on whether the Fed would provide the kind of support it gave money market funds in 2008, Warsh stated 'We do not want to be in the bailout business, full stop.' He added that the Fed would 'do everything we can to mitigate... extraordinary risks' but would not bail out crypto. He did not fully rule out marginal systemic-spillover mitigation. (2) GENIUS Act rulemaking urgency: Warsh told lawmakers the Fed is 'racing' to finalize its portion of the GENIUS Act stablecoin implementing rules ahead of the July 18, 2026 one-year statutory deadline. The deadline has since been confirmed missed (the Federal Register contains no in-scope publication; July 18 is a Saturday; earliest possible publication is Monday July 20). (3) Nonbank fintech payment-system access: Rep. Sherman separately pressed on Kraken's pending bank application and nonbank crypto firms seeking direct access to the payment system; Warsh invoked systemic-risk considerations without making a specific commitment. Background: Warsh is the most crypto-sympathetic Fed Chair on record, having previously disclosed venture stakes in Bitcoin payments, a crypto index manager, Bitwise, and a stablecoin venture â all divested under Fed ethics rules prior to confirmation in May 2026. A 2026 New York Fed staff report cited in contemporaneous coverage found stablecoin activity can transmit liquidity stress to banks and complicate monetary policy. This is Warsh's first congressional testimony since his confirmation. Secondary coverage: Law360, July 14, 2026 ('Fed Racing To Hit Genius Act Rules Deadline, Warsh Says'); CCN via Yahoo Finance, July 15, 2026 ('Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Says Crypto and Stablecoins Are On Their Own in a Crisis').
items.source_label: Federal Reserve Board â Semiannual Monetary Policy Report Testimony, Chairman Kevin Warsh, House Committee on Financial Services, July 14, 2026
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, crypto banks, nonbank payment providers, fintech firms seeking Fed master accounts, crypto exchanges with pending bank applications

items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
items.title: CFTC Approves Water Street Labs, LLC as New Designated Contract Market for Fully Collateralized Event Contract Products
items.facts: The CFTC approved Water Street Labs, LLC's application to become a designated contract market (DCM), as reported by Gambling Insider and DeFiRate (July 17, 2026). Both reports attribute the approval to an official CFTC designation order. According to the reports, Water Street Labs plans to offer fully collateralized products through both a central limit order book and a parimutuel auction model. No formal CFTC press release number was located on cftc.gov corresponding to this designation at time of publication.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider â Prediction Markets Weekly Roundup (July 17, 2026), corroborated by DeFiRate
items.relevant_to: Prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, fintech operators in the derivatives and event-contracts space

items.issuing_body: U.S. House Committee on Financial Services, Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence
items.title: House Financial Services digital assets subcommittee convenes CLARITY Act field hearing at Federal Hall, with H.Res. 111 and the American Reserve Modernization Act noticed
items.facts: The U.S. House Committee on Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence noticed a field hearing titled 'Building the Future of Finance: How the CLARITY Act Unlocks Innovation' for Friday, July 17, 2026 at 10:00 AM local time at Federal Hall National Memorial, 15 Pine Street, New York, NY. The Committee Repository entry for the hearing was first published July 10, 2026 and last updated July 15, 2026, when witness testimony, Truth in Testimony forms, and biographies were posted. Four witnesses are listed: Sarah Aberg, Chief Legal Officer, Nova Labs Inc.; Randi Abernethy, Head of Clearing and Group Risk, Bullish; Ryan Louvar, Chief Legal Officer, WisdomTree; and Jason Somensatto, Director of Policy, Coin Center. Two measures are noticed as text of legislation for the hearing: H.Res. 111, 'Expressing support for blockchain technology and digital assets,' and H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act. A hearing notice and a committee memorandum are posted as support documents. The hearing is a legislative hearing; no markup, vote, or committee action on the CLARITY Act is noticed on the event page.
items.source_label: U.S. House Committee Repository — hearing event page (notice, witness testimony, and noticed legislation), July 17, 2026
items.relevant_to: digital asset exchanges, token issuers, custodians, stablecoin issuers, crypto market infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: North Carolina Supreme Court (amicus filers: NC Sheriffs' Association, NC Association of Chiefs of Police, NC Conference of District Attorneys, NC Family Policy Council)
items.title: NC Law Enforcement Groups and Family Policy Council File Amicus Briefs Against Video Sweepstakes Operator at NC Supreme Court; Oral Arguments Set for September 2026
items.facts: On July 16, 2026, the North Carolina Sheriffs' Association, North Carolina Association of Chiefs of Police, and North Carolina Conference of District Attorneys filed a joint amicus brief in No Limit Games v. Sheriff of Robeson County at the North Carolina Supreme Court, urging the court to uphold the Court of Appeals' 2-1 December 2024 ruling that No Limit Games' video sweepstakes devices violate N.C. Gen. Stat. Â§ 14-306.4. The North Carolina Family Policy Council filed a separate amicus brief the same day. Oral arguments are scheduled for September 2026. The case involves whether No Limit's sweepstakes system â which includes an optional skill-based 'Instant Reveal' function â falls outside the statutory prohibition on video games of chance used in the entry or reveal of sweepstakes prizes. A trial court granted an injunction in No Limit's favor in 2023; the Court of Appeals reversed 2-1 in December 2024.
items.source_label: Carolina Journal â Video sweepstakes case at top NC court attracts outside interest (July 16, 2026); amicus briefs filed at ncappellatecourts.org
items.relevant_to: Sweepstakes casino operators, skill-gaming platforms, gaming companies with North Carolina exposure

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
items.title: CFTC stays KalshiEX rule change and uses emergency authority to order fulfillment of Michigan trades a state court directed be canceled (Release 9267-26)
items.facts: On July 14, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced (Release 9267-26) that it exercised its authority to stay an emergency rule change proposed by KalshiEX, LLC in response to a Michigan state court order directing the company to cancel certain previously executed trades involving Michigan residents, and separately exercised its emergency authority to order KalshiEX to fulfill the open trades in accordance with its normal practices. Chairman Michael S. Selig stated that 'a state cannot force a DCM to violate its obligations, and federal law does not permit a DCM to discriminate against a state's residents,' and called canceling already-executed trades an 'unprecedented step' that risks a cascading effect on the marketplace. The Commission noted that Michigan is the first state to attempt to interfere directly with executed derivatives transactions and that it has filed lawsuits against Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin to protect its jurisdiction.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9267-26 (July 14, 2026; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms and event-contract DCMs, designated contract markets, state gaming regulators, exchanges operating across state lines

items.issuing_body: U.S. Treasury — Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
items.title: OFAC sanctions ransomware-supporting malware and infrastructure providers, adding numerous cryptocurrency wallet addresses to the SDN List
items.facts: On July 13, 2026, the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control added individuals and an entity to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under its cyber-related authority (CYBER4) for supporting ransomware attacks against Americans, including Ukrainian national Dmytro Rashevskyi, Belarusian national Yevgeniy Vladimirovich Silayev, and the entity First VPN Service (Dnipro, Ukraine). The designations list multiple blocked cryptocurrency wallet addresses spanning Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, Zcash, Dash, Tron, Dogecoin, and Solana. The action was announced alongside separate Cuba-related designations and a new Cuba-related FAQ (FAQ 1262); the related Treasury press release is SB0559.
items.source_label: OFAC Recent Actions — Cyber-related Designations (July 13, 2026; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges and VASPs, blockchain analytics and compliance teams, custodians, payment processors screening sanctioned wallets

items.issuing_body: KalshiEX LLC / U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York (No. 25-cv-08846-AT, Judge Analisa Torres)
items.title: Kalshi Seeks Emergency Injunction Pending Appeal in SDNY Case; New York Agrees to No-Enforcement Standstill Through July 30, Kalshi to Seek Second Circuit Relief July 23
items.facts: On July 15, 2026, KalshiEX LLC filed a letter motion in KalshiEX LLC v. Williams (No. 25-cv-08846-AT, S.D.N.Y., Judge Analisa Torres) seeking an emergency injunction pending appeal of the court's prior denial of a preliminary injunction. The filing states that defendants (New York state officials) agreed not to bring an enforcement action against Kalshi under New York law through July 30, 2026, while the motion is pending. If the court does not grant relief, Kalshi intends to seek a Second Circuit injunction pending appeal on July 23, 2026. The motion argues that the case presents serious legal questions about whether the Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gambling laws, noting the Third Circuit ruled for Kalshi in KalshiEX LLC v. Flaherty (172 F.4th 220, 3d Cir. 2026), while a separate federal preemption suit (CFTC v. New York, No. 26-cv-3404, S.D.N.Y., Judge Marrero) is pending in the same district. Source: primary court document (Docket 110, letter motion filed by Grant Mainland, Milbank) retrieved via CourtListener/RECAP.
items.source_label: KalshiEX LLC v. Williams, No. 25-cv-08846-AT (S.D.N.Y.) â Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal, filed July 15, 2026 (via CourtListener/RECAP, Docket 110)
items.relevant_to: Prediction-market platforms, CFTC-registered exchanges, gaming operators with New York exposure

items.issuing_body: OCC / FDIC / NCUA / U.S. Treasury / FinCEN / OFAC
items.title: GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline (July 18, 2026) one week out — six agencies had not finalized implementing rules as of July 11
items.facts: As of July 11, 2026, six federal agencies — the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), the U.S. Treasury Department, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) — faced a statutory July 18, 2026 deadline (one year after the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2025 enactment) to finalize implementing rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), and had not yet issued final rules. Comment periods on the proposed rules closed by early June 2026. The proposed framework requires PPSIs to hold 1:1 reserves in cash, insured deposits, and short-term U.S. Treasuries, and treats issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act. Source: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers (Chapman & Cutler, Paradigm).
items.source_label: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers
items.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, banks and credit unions entering stablecoins, digital-asset custodians, BSA/AML compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
items.title: SEC regulatory agenda targets July 2026 for three crypto rulemakings (digital-asset offerings, broker-dealer custody, market structure)
items.facts: Per The Cryptonomist (July 11, 2026) citing the SEC's RegInfo Unified Agenda, the Securities and Exchange Commission has set July 2026 targets for three crypto rule proposals: (1) digital-asset offerings — a Division of Corporation Finance rulemaking that may include exemptions or safe harbors (legal authority listed as 'not yet determined'); (2) broker-dealer financial-responsibility, custody, and recordkeeping amendments (Rules 15c3-1, 15c3-3, 17a-3, 17a-4); and (3) market-structure amendments for crypto trading venues. As of July 11, 2026, no proposal had appeared in the Federal Register; the RegInfo entries reflect agenda-stage targets, not filed NPRMs. Corroborated by Decrypt, The Industry Spread, and Yahoo Finance.
items.source_label: The Cryptonomist (July 11, 2026), citing the SEC RegInfo Unified Agenda; corroborated by Decrypt, The Industry Spread, Yahoo Finance
items.relevant_to: crypto token issuers, broker-dealers, digital-asset custodians, crypto trading venues, exchanges

items.issuing_body: U.S. Congress (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, H.R.6644 §1101)
items.title: First U.S. statutory ban on a Federal Reserve CBDC takes effect via the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644 §1101)
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644) became law without President Trump's signature. Per coverage by The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026), corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026), Section 1101 prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC) or any substantially similar digital asset, directly or through an intermediary, through December 31, 2030. The bill passed the Senate 85-5 (June 22, 2026) and the House 358-32. Coverage reports a carve-out for open, permissionless, privately issued dollar-denominated digital assets (understood by coverage to include stablecoins). Statutory text cited by coverage but not independently retrieved. This supersedes and follows the Senate-passage entry (2026-06-19-senate-passes-road-housing-cbdc-ban) and bill-text entry (2026-06-18-congress-cbdc-ban-road-to-housing-act).
items.source_label: The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026); corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026); statute text not independently retrieved
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency)
items.title: OCC grants Circle final approval for a national trust bank charter (First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. / Circle National Trust)
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted Circle Internet Group final approval to establish First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (operating as Circle National Trust), a national trust bank that will provide fiduciary digital-asset custody for Circle and its affiliates. Circle applied to the OCC on June 30, 2025 and received conditional approval in December 2025 before final approval on July 10, 2026. As reported, this is the first national trust bank charter granted to a stablecoin issuer; Circle plans for the bank to serve as the primary custodial entity for USDC reserves and related digital-asset custody functions. Source: Circle press release (July 10, 2026); corroborated by American Banker, CoinDesk, CNBC, and BusinessWire. OCC decision letter not independently retrieved.
items.source_label: Circle Press Release (July 10, 2026); corroborated by American Banker, CoinDesk, CNBC, BusinessWire; OCC decision letter not independently retrieved
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, digital-asset custodians, national trust banks, crypto-native firms pursuing federal charters

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (Banking Committee / Agriculture Committee)
items.title: Merged Senate CLARITY Act draft expected week of July 20; ethics provision remains the sticking point; no text filed as of July 9
items.facts: CoinDesk reported (July 9, 2026) that a new merged version of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — combining Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts, with reportedly more than 70 pages added — could be released as soon as the week of July 20, 2026 for potential Senate floor action. Per the reporting, the draft had not secured the Democratic support needed for 60 votes to clear a filibuster; the main open issue was an ethics provision restricting senior officials, including the president, from crypto business ties, with federal preemption rules and SEC/CFTC commissioner nominations also unresolved. No bill text had been filed as of July 9, 2026.
items.source_label: CoinDesk (July 9, 2026)
items.relevant_to: crypto market-structure stakeholders, exchanges, token issuers, CFTC/SEC-regulated venues, DeFi protocols

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / HM Treasury
items.title: U.S.-UK Transatlantic Taskforce publishes recommendations on capital markets and digital assets, plus a joint statement on stablecoins
items.facts: On July 14, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury and HM Treasury jointly published recommendations of the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future (Treasury press release SB0560). Treasury states the recommendations aim to deepen cross-border financial activity between the United States and the United Kingdom, reduce unnecessary frictions, and advance open, market-based standards, and that they identify opportunities to enhance cross-border capital raising, update supervisory cooperation, and provide clarity for tokenized financial activity. Following one of the Taskforce's recommendations, the United States and the UK released a joint statement on stablecoins the same day, which Treasury says supports dynamic cross-border stablecoin activity and highlights the key role of the private sector in the provision of money and payments. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Taskforce 'reflects the strength and depth of U.S. and UK markets and our shared commitment to fostering economic growth and advancing global standards that reward innovation and competition.' The Taskforce was established by Secretary Bessent and UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves in September 2025 and is co-chaired by U.S. Treasury and HM Treasury with participants from U.S. and UK financial sector regulatory agencies.
items.source_label: U.S. Treasury Press Release SB0560 (July 14, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment processors, tokenization platforms with U.S.-UK footprints

items.issuing_body: Ingham County Circuit Court (Michigan) — Judge Rosemarie Aquilina
items.title: Michigan judge extends Kalshi sports-contract restraining order and sets Aug. 12 geofencing deadline with $500,000-per-day fines
items.facts: As reported by Legal Sports Report and Gaming America on July 14, 2026, Ingham County Circuit Court Judge Rosemarie Aquilina heard arguments from the State of Michigan and KalshiEX on Monday, July 13, 2026, and extended the temporary restraining order against Kalshi's sports event contracts without setting an expiration date, ordering Kalshi to geofence the state by the end of day August 12, 2026. Per that coverage, if Kalshi does not geofence by that date it could face a $500,000 daily fine for violating the order, and Aquilina said Kalshi could also be punished under the initial $120,000-per-day penalties if it delays within the 30-day period, stating 'If you sit on it for 29 days, there will be sanctions.' Kalshi argued it falls under CFTC and Commodity Exchange Act regulation; Aquilina found conflict preemption did not apply because Kalshi can comply with both state and federal law simultaneously. The parties are scheduled to appear in court again the following week. The written order was not published on a free public docket and was not retrieved.
items.source_label: Legal Sports Report (July 14, 2026); corroborated by Gaming America (July 14, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, gaming operators with Michigan users

items.issuing_body: Independent Community Bankers of America / American Bankers Association
items.title: ICBA, ABA and 76 state banking associations urge Senate leaders to tighten CLARITY Act Section 404 stablecoin yield provisions
items.facts: As announced by the Independent Community Bankers of America on July 13, 2026, the American Bankers Association and ICBA, joined by 76 state associations, sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Charles Schumer urging targeted changes to the CLARITY Act to provide greater certainty that payment stablecoins cannot function as substitutes for bank deposits. The associations wrote that 'significant questions remain regarding whether the current language in Section 404 provides sufficient clarity and certainty to achieve that objective' and that 'ambiguities within the bill could encourage stablecoin arrangements to effectively function as substitutes for deposits, despite Congress's longstanding and clearly stated intent that payment stablecoins should serve as transaction tools rather than store-of-value products.' They urge revisions clarifying the prohibition on interest and yield, replacing the bill's 'functional and economic equivalent' standard with a 'substantially similar' standard, and removing language they believe could create ambiguity regarding rewards tied to stablecoin balances, duration or tenure. The underlying letter is linked from the announcement and was not independently retrieved.
items.source_label: ICBA announcement (July 13, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, exchanges running rewards programs, payments and fintech operators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate / Senate Banking & Agriculture Committees (via staff)
items.title: CLARITY Act: Senate staff expected to release unified crypto market-structure draft this week; floor vote targeted July 20; August 7 recess is the hard deadline — passage odds at 50%
items.facts: Multiple credible outlets (crypto.news, TechTimes, The Hill) reported on July 11-12, 2026 that Senate staff are expected to release a unified draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) during the week of July 13, 2026, merging parallel Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts. Floor action is targeted for the week of July 20. The Senate leaves for its August recess on August 7, 2026, leaving approximately three working weeks. Galaxy Research has reduced 2026 passage odds to 50%, citing calendar compression, down from 60% earlier in July. Three disputes remain unresolved: (1) ethics/conflict-of-interest rules covering senior officials with crypto holdings; (2) CFTC commissioner vacancies; (3) Section 604 blockchain developer shield. H.R. 3633 passed the House 294-134 on July 17, 2025; cleared Senate Banking Committee 15-9 on May 14, 2026; placed on Senate Calendar No. 423 on June 1, 2026.
items.source_label: crypto.news via Cryptonews.net — 'Three weeks to 2030: the seven-Democrat math that decides the CLARITY Act', July 11 2026 (corroborated by TechTimes July 12 and The Hill July 1)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital-asset operators, DeFi builders, token issuers, fintech operators, institutional investors

items.issuing_body: Arizona Department of Gaming
items.title: Arizona Department of Gaming issues cease-and-desist orders to five online gambling operators alleging felony promotion of gambling, illegal control of an enterprise, and money laundering
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the Arizona Department of Gaming announced it had issued cease-and-desist orders to BetOpenly, Bookmaker, Club WPT Online Poker, Kutt Inc., and Raffle Creator, with each enforcement action alleging conduct giving rise to the felonies of promotion of gambling, illegal control of an enterprise, and money laundering. The Department alleges, among other things, that BetOpenly enabled event wagering and daily fantasy sports contests without the requisite state licenses and facilitated availability to underage Arizonans; that Bookmaker facilitated wagering on horse racing, casino games, and sports betting without an event wagering or advanced deposit wagering provider license; that Club WPT Online Poker enabled Arizonans under 21 to engage in pay-to-play online poker tournaments for prizes while using deceptive 'no purchase necessary' language; that Kutt Inc. allowed Arizona users to deposit money and wager on sports, politics, pop culture and casino-style games in a manner providing prohibited third-party benefit; and that Raffle Creator allowed people under 21 to purchase raffle tickets for prizes without meeting Arizona nonprofit raffle requirements. Notified entities are directed to immediately stop all gambling operations and activities in Arizona and to desist from future illegal gambling operations; the Department states future actions may include criminal charges or civil action against entities, principals, and employees, potential restitution awards, and forfeiture of all monies acquired due to the illegal conduct. Department Director Jackie Johnson said, 'Through these cease-and-desist orders we are putting operators on notice: their conduct runs contrary to Arizona law and they must stop promoting illegal gambling.' All conduct described is alleged by the Department and unadjudicated.
items.source_label: Arizona Department of Gaming press release (July 10, 2026)
items.relevant_to: sweepstakes and social-casino operators, online sportsbooks, DFS and raffle platforms

items.issuing_body: North Carolina Office of the Governor
items.title: North Carolina Governor Stein signs $34B SB 257 budget enacting 6% prediction-market tax on net trading-fee revenue, effective 2027
items.facts: On July 8, 2026, North Carolina Governor Josh Stein signed Senate Bill 257, the state's approximately $34 billion fiscal year 2026 budget. As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the enacted budget includes a 6% tax on the net trading fee revenue earned by prediction market operators with North Carolina users; platforms named in reporting include Kalshi and Polymarket. The tax is scheduled to take effect in 2027. The enacted budget does not impose state gambling licensing, know-your-customer, or responsible-gaming requirements on prediction-market platforms. This item supersedes the July 6 item (2026-07-06-north-carolina-prediction-market-tax), which covered SB 257 at conference committee stage; the Governor's signing converts it to enacted law.
items.source_label: GamblingNews (July 8, 2026; reporting the Governor's signing of SB 257)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sports-betting operators, tax and compliance teams serving operators with North Carolina users

items.issuing_body: New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee
items.title: New Jersey Senate Budget Committee approves amended S4447 (9% prediction-market gross income tax) 9-4; amended bill explicitly recognizes CFTC as federal regulator
items.facts: As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee approved amendments to S4447 by a 9-4 vote. The amended bill imposes a 9% tax on prediction market gross income for operators offering event contracts to New Jersey residents. The amended version explicitly recognizes the CFTC as the federal regulator of prediction markets and drops prior self-exclusion requirements. The New Jersey Office of Legislative Services estimated the tax would generate approximately $10.3 million to $15.3 million annually. The bill requires a full Senate vote, Assembly action, and the Governor's signature before becoming law.
items.source_label: GamblingNews (July 8, 2026; reporting the Committee vote on S4447)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, tax and compliance teams, payment processors serving operators with New Jersey users

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York
items.title: SDNY judge denies Kalshi's preliminary injunction against the New York State Gaming Commission; holds the CEA does not preempt state gambling laws as applied to sports-event contracts
items.facts: On July 7, 2026, U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres (S.D.N.Y.) denied KalshiEX LLC's motion for a preliminary injunction in KalshiEX LLC v. Williams (No. 1:25-cv-08846), a suit against the New York State Gaming Commission. The order states that 'New York gambling laws as applied to Kalshi's sports-event contracts are not preempted by the CEA and Kalshi has not, therefore, made a clear or substantial showing that it is likely to succeed on the merits.' The court declined to read the Commodity Exchange Act's grant of exclusive jurisdiction as leaving no room for state gambling regulation, found Kalshi's alleged injuries were largely monetary, and noted that nothing prevents Kalshi from obtaining a license under New York law. As reported by The Block (July 8, 2026), Kalshi has appealed the decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.
items.source_label: The Block (July 8, 2026), reporting and quoting the S.D.N.Y. order (docket 1:25-cv-08846, ECF No. 106); court order not independently retrieved
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, state-licensed gaming operators, CFTC-registered DCMs

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC charges North Carolina commodity pool operator and company with fraud involving crypto assets and equity index futures ($14M+, 60+ victims)
items.facts: On July 7, 2026, the CFTC filed a civil enforcement complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina (Press Release 9264-26) against Trevor L. Vernon and Argent Capital Management LLC. The complaint alleges that from approximately March 2022 through February 2026, Vernon and Argent Capital solicited approximately $14 million from more than 60 participants for a commodity pool that purported to trade equity index futures contracts, options on equity index futures, and crypto assets, among other purported investments. The CFTC alleges Vernon misappropriated pool funds and operated a Ponzi-like scheme, making lulling payments to earlier participants with funds from newer investors. The complaint seeks restitution, civil monetary penalties, disgorgement, and permanent trading and registration bans.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9264-26 (July 7, 2026; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: commodity pool operators, crypto asset traders, CFTC-registered entities, CPO compliance programs, investment fraud compliance teams

items.issuing_body: Nevada Supreme Court
items.title: Nevada Supreme Court denies Kalshi's emergency stay, leaving geofencing mandate in force as July 16 contempt hearing is set
items.facts: As reported by CoinDesk and Tech Times (July 5, 2026), the Nevada Supreme Court on or about July 1, 2026 denied KalshiEx, LLC's emergency motion for a stay pending appeal, so Kalshi must continue to geofence and block Nevada users from prohibited event contracts while the state's lawsuit proceeds. Per the coverage, a three-justice panel (Linda Marie Bell, Ron D. Parraguirre, and Kristina Pickering) said it was 'not persuaded' by the emergency motion. Separately, the Nevada Gaming Control Board has asked the First Judicial District Court to hold Kalshi in contempt for allegedly failing to geofence the state, and a full-day evidentiary hearing on that question is scheduled for July 16, 2026.
items.source_label: CoinDesk (citing Nevada Supreme Court docket)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, sportsbook operators

items.issuing_body: North Carolina General Assembly
items.title: North Carolina budget deal (SB 257) adds a 6% tax on prediction-market trading-fee revenue, without bringing platforms under state gambling rules
items.facts: As reported by CoinDesk and Tech Times (July 5, 2026) and corroborated by WRAL and Bloomberg Tax, North Carolina lawmakers included a 6% tax on prediction-market operators' net in-state trading-fee revenue in the state's roughly $34 billion conference budget bill (SB 257), reported the week of June 30-July 2, 2026. Per the coverage, the tax would take effect in 2027 and apply to platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, but the budget language does not place prediction-market platforms under North Carolina's gambling licensing, know-your-customer, or responsible-gaming rules; the same budget raises the state's online sports-betting tax from 18% to 23%.
items.source_label: CoinDesk (citing N.C. General Assembly budget bill SB 257)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sports-betting operators, tax and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Supreme Court
items.title: SCOTUS rules 6-3 that for-cause removal protections for SEC and CFTC commissioners are unconstitutional (Trump v. Slaughter, No. 25-332)
items.facts: On June 29, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States issued its 6-3 opinion in Trump v. Slaughter (No. 25-332), authored by Chief Justice Roberts, overturning Humphrey's Executor v. United States (1935). The Court held that the for-cause removal protection in the FTC's enabling statute — and by structural extension the SEC and CFTC, which operate under identical removal provisions — is contrary to the separation of powers under the Constitution. Effective immediately, the President may remove SEC and CFTC commissioners without cause. A companion order in Trump v. Cook (No. 25A312, June 29, 2026) denied a government application to stay a preliminary injunction protecting Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook; the Federal Reserve's statutory structure was not directly addressed by the majority opinion. The opinion is published on the Court's official slip opinion list for October Term 2025.
items.source_label: U.S. Supreme Court — Official Slip Opinion List, October Term 2025 (primary source; retrieved July 3, 2026); Opinion PDF: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/25-322_new_4gcj.pdf
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital asset issuers, fintech platforms, prediction-market operators, CFTC-registered entities, and all operators subject to SEC or CFTC jurisdiction

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate
items.title: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) misses July 4 Senate floor vote target as bipartisan talks collapse
items.facts: As of July 2, 2026, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) did not receive a Senate floor vote before the July 4 recess deadline targeted by White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt. According to the Bitcoin Foundation (July 2, 2026; corroborated by Elliptic, Crypto.news, PYMNTS, and Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto), bipartisan negotiations failed to secure the minimum 7 Democratic votes needed to clear the Senate's 60-vote cloture threshold. Outstanding disputes included DeFi oversight provisions, stablecoin rewards provisions, AML reporting requirements, and Section 604 (Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act). The bill remains on the Senate Legislative Calendar (General Orders, Calendar No. 423) and is not dead; a floor vote has been pushed to after the July 4 recess at earliest. Multiple trade outlets reported prediction market passage odds fell from approximately 74% approximately one month prior to approximately 48% as of the July 2 reporting date.
items.source_label: Bitcoin Foundation, July 2, 2026 (corroborated by Elliptic, Crypto.news, PYMNTS, Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, token platforms, stablecoin issuers, DeFi protocols, fintech and payments operators awaiting US market structure clarity

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
items.title: OFAC adds Monero (XMR) and 100+ TRON addresses to ISIS-K SDN entry; designates Brazilian payments company Pixwave under SDGT and narco-trafficking EO
items.facts: On July 1, 2026, OFAC published two actions on its recent-actions page. First, OFAC updated the existing SDGT entry for ISIS-K to add three Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency wallet addresses and more than 100 TRON (TRC-20) blockchain addresses — including USDT-TRC20 stablecoin addresses — to the SDN List. Second, OFAC designated Pixwave Soluções de Pagamentos Ltda, a Brazilian payment-technology company, under the SDGT authority (E.O. 13224) and Executive Order 14059 (ILLICIT-DRUGS-EO14059), alleging Pixwave provided payment-processing services to the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), a Brazilian narco-trafficking organization. Both designations are effective July 1, 2026.
items.source_label: OFAC Recent Actions — July 1, 2026 (primary source; retrieved)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, virtual asset service providers (VASPs), payment processors, money transmitters, and any US person transacting in Monero or TRON-chain assets (including USDT-TRC20)

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
items.title: SEC seeks public comment on registration and disclosure rules for novel exchange-traded funds (Release 33-11426) — crypto-asset and event-contract ETFs expressly in scope
items.facts: On June 30, 2026, the SEC released Release 33-11426, a request for public comment on potential amendments to its registration and disclosure rules for novel types of exchange-traded funds, including crypto-asset ETFs and ETFs holding event-contract or prediction-market exposures. The release asks whether current disclosure frameworks adequately address risks specific to non-standard ETF product types and whether the Commission should take additional steps, including potential Commission-initiated delay of automatic effectiveness of registration statements under Rule 485. Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication.
items.source_label: SEC Press Release (June 30, 2026) — Release 33-11426
items.relevant_to: crypto-asset ETF sponsors, investment companies, fund managers, broker-dealers, prediction-market ETF applicants

items.title: SEC obtains $5.4M default judgment against NanoBit Limited for operating a fake cryptocurrency trading platform (pig-butchering / relationship-investment scam)
items.facts: On June 25, 2026, the SDNY entered a final judgment by default against NanoBit Limited and co-defendants in SEC v. NanoBit Limited et al. (No. 1:24-cv-09413). NanoBit operated a fraudulent cryptocurrency trading platform where victims were recruited through social media and dating apps. The final default judgment orders disgorgement, prejudgment interest, and civil monetary penalties totaling approximately $5.4 million. The SEC published the order as Litigation Release No. LR-26576 on June 29, 2026.

items.facts: As reported by The Guardian (June 28, 2026), the ICBA launched a six-figure advertising campaign in Washington D.C. opposing CLARITY Act provisions that would allow stablecoin issuers to pay yield on holdings. items.issuing_body: KalshiEx LLC (plaintiff) v. Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Illinois Gaming Board — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois
items.title: Kalshi files federal lawsuit against Illinois over SB3019's 15% sports prediction market gross receipts tax and state licensing requirement for DCMs; TRO and PI sought ahead of July 1 effective date
items.facts: Kalshi filed a 31-page federal complaint in the N.D. Illinois on June 23, 2026. SB3019 imposes: (a) a 15% gross-receipts tax on sports prediction market revenues; (b) a state licensing requirement for CFTC-registered DCMs. Both provisions took effect July 1, 2026. Kalshi argues both provisions are preempted by the Commodity Exchange Act's exclusive-jurisdiction clause (7 U.S.C. § 2(a)(1)(A)). The complaint seeks a TRO, preliminary injunction, and permanent injunction.

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC issues Request for Information on fintech innovation, AI, and digital asset technologies (Release 9254-26)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the CFTC issued Release 9254-26, a Request for Information on fintech innovation, AI, and digital asset technologies. The RFI covers DeFi protocols, AI/ML applications in trading, RWA tokenization, payment stablecoins as margin/collateral, and cybersecurity.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9254-26
items.relevant_to: DeFi protocols, crypto exchanges, stablecoin issuers, AI trading firms, RWA tokenization platforms

items.issuing_body: Pennsylvania Supreme Court
items.title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court rules skill games are slot machines; 120-day enforcement stay issued
items.facts: On June 15, 2026, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court issued its majority opinion in J-97-2025 (Pace-O-Matic v. Pennsylvania), ruling that skill game machines 'are subject to both the Gaming Act and the Crimes Code,' overturning a Commonwealth Court ruling. The Court issued a 120-day enforcement stay.
items.source_label: Pennsylvania Supreme Court Opinion J-97-2025 (majority opinion)
items.relevant_to: skill game operators, gaming venues (bars, VFWs, fraternal clubs), payment processors, PA legislators

items.issuing_body: Financial Technology Association v. Tennessee — Davidson County Chancery Court
items.title: Fintech trade group sues Tennessee to block remittance tax (HB2502)
items.facts: The Financial Technology Association filed suit in Davidson County (Tennessee) Chancery Court seeking an injunction to block HB2502, a law signed by Gov. Bill Lee in May 2026 that adds a $10 fee on monetary wire transfers abroad plus a 2% tax on transfers over $500 (effective Jan. 1, 2027). The FTA argues the law is unconstitutional under the dormant Commerce Clause.
items.source_label: The Center Square (reporting the FTA v. Tennessee filing)
items.relevant_to: money transmitters, remittance providers, payment processors, fintechs

items.issuing_body: Delaware General Assembly (HB 441) / New Jersey Legislature (S-2141)
items.title: Delaware (HB 441) and New Jersey (S-2141) advance statewide crypto-ATM bans
items.facts: Delaware and New Jersey have each advanced legislation to ban cryptocurrency ATMs statewide, citing fraud losses. Delaware's HB 441 passed the House; it would require existing kiosks to go dark upon enactment and be physically removed within 90 days. New Jersey's S-2141 cleared the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Delaware and New Jersey crypto-ATM ban bills)
items.relevant_to: crypto-ATM/kiosk operators, payment processors, compliance vendors

items.issuing_body: Gary Gensler (amicus) — U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Gensler files Sixth Circuit amicus arguing sports prediction markets are not 'swaps'
items.facts: On 2026-06-11, former CFTC and SEC chair Gary Gensler filed an amicus brief with the Sixth Circuit in KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler, arguing that sports-event prediction-market contracts fall outside the statutory definition of a 'swap' under Dodd-Frank and are therefore not within the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Gensler Sixth Circuit amicus brief)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, derivatives exchanges, crypto exchanges

items.issuing_body: State of Wisconsin (Attorney General) — U.S. District Court, W.D. Wis.
items.title: Wisconsin moves to block sports event-contract trading on Coinbase, Kalshi, and Robinhood
items.facts: On 2026-06-09, the State of Wisconsin filed a motion for a preliminary injunction seeking to block KalshiEx, Coinbase, and Robinhood from offering sports event-contract trading to people in the state.
items.source_label: DeFi Rate (reporting the Wisconsin preliminary-injunction motion)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, crypto exchanges, brokerages

items.issuing_body: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
items.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
items.facts: On 2026-06-12, the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's NADEX, Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the Coalition for Fair Markets filing; first reported by the Associated Press)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, licensed gaming operators, payment processors

items.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board
items.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada.
items.source_label: Las Vegas Review-Journal (reporting the Nevada GCB court filing)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, geolocation/compliance vendors, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9251-26
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges, CFTC registrants
